sum: T-Mobile US reported stronger operating and financial performance for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, while raising key full-year cash-flow and profitability targets. The company also introduced T-Mix wireless plans and a 5 Gig fiber offer as it seeks to deepen customer relationships beyond mobile service.

In its October 28 earnings release, T-Mobile US said total service revenue rose 6 percent year over year to 19.4 billion US dollars. Postpaid service revenue increased 9 percent to 16.3 billion US dollars, while net income climbed 27 percent to 3.5 billion US dollars.

The company attributed the performance to postpaid net account and postpaid average revenue per account growth that exceeded its original expectations. The release also reported diluted earnings per share of 3.22 US dollars, up 34 percent from a year earlier.

T-Mobile US lifted its full-year core adjusted EBITDA outlook to between 37.35 billion and 37.45 billion US dollars. The midpoint is higher than the previous range of 37.1 billion to 37.5 billion US dollars. Adjusted free cash flow, including payments linked to the UScellular merger, is now expected to range from 18.7 billion to 18.8 billion US dollars, compared with a previous range of 18.4 billion to 18.8 billion US dollars.

The company’s commercial push continued on November 2. T-Mobile announced a 5 Gig T-Mobile Fiber plan priced at 90 US dollars per month with AutoPay, plus taxes and fees. The offer includes a 10-year price guarantee and became available on November 3.

T-Mobile also said T-Mix plans would let customers choose benefits across categories such as streaming, music, gaming, travel and food delivery, with the ability to change their mix as needs evolve. The strategy is designed to give the carrier more ways to bundle wireless, broadband and digital services.

For investors, the latest developments reinforce a growth narrative built on postpaid account expansion, higher customer spending and additional broadband products. The main execution question is whether richer benefits and promotional offers can attract and retain customers without putting undue pressure on margins or increasing churn.

sum: T-Mobile US has seen its share price move around over the past few years, and that raises a straightforward question for you as an investor: Is the current valuation of T-Mobile US stock properly grounded in the earnings the business is generating today?
Over the past 5 years the stock has returned 39.4%, which puts quite a bit of weight on whether the current earnings power can support that journey so far.

Recent reports on cybersecurity upgrades, network performance and new fiber offerings may support expectations around future profitability and the timing of cash flows, which all feed back into how much investors are prepared to pay for each dollar of earnings.
The issue now is whether T-Mobile US stock at around US$160 per share is appropriately aligned with what its earnings justify.
If you are weighing T-Mobile US against other telecoms on earnings and cash flow resilience, it can help to line it up next to 29 resilient stocks with low risk scores.

The P/E ratio is a useful shorthand for T-Mobile US because earnings are now a central focus for how investors value large wireless carriers. At around 15.0x earnings, the stock trades very close to the Wireless Telecom industry average of about 14.9x. This frames it as broadly in line with the sector on this single measure.

Against a broader peer set that averages roughly 33.6x, T-Mobile US changes hands at a much lower multiple, so the market is not pricing it like the higher rated telecom and adjacent players. A fair P/E based on a more tailored model that considers T-Mobile US specific growth profile, margins, size and risk comes out above the current ratio. This points to the shares screening undervalued on this framework. Because the company recently reported higher earnings and raised its profitability outlook, that discount on P/E may catch the eye of investors comparing it with other telecom stocks. Why Did T-Mobile Stock Jump?
sum: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

T-Mobile US (TMUS) shares gained 6.2% on Friday, October 30, 2026, while the S&P 500 lost 1.8%. The company released no announcements, earnings reports, or filings that day. A news report linked the gain to fresh estimates of what it could cost SpaceX to build a rival U.S. mobile carrier. Why would SpaceX’s plans matter to T-Mobile?

SpaceX is weighing an entry into the U.S. mobile market where T-Mobile operates. That potential entry has hung over wireless stocks, one article said on October 30. Another article that day said higher cost estimates for the project were lifting the carriers SpaceX hopes to challenge, with T-Mobile among them.
T-Mobile has already ruled out one way in. On its October 28 earnings call, management said it sees no room for SpaceX to run a mobile service on T-Mobile’s network.

SpaceX would compete for the customers T-Mobile counted in that day’s report. During the third quarter of 2026, the company added 274,000 postpaid accounts. Management calls these monthly-bill customers the all-important part of its business, and its postpaid service revenue grew 9% from a year earlier. The shares slipped 0.5% in the session after that report.

T-Mobile moved with its peers and against the market. AT&T, Verizon, Comcast, Charter and Telephone and Data Systems, the companies on its Trefis peer list, all rose in the same session, with Comcast up 4.3% and AT&T up 2.3%. The SPDR fund that tracks its sector, communication services, fell 1.3%.

No session in the prior 365 days brought T-Mobile a rise this large. The latest big move went the other way: a 7.7% fall on October 23, which left the shares at $146.54, their lowest close of the past year. That fall came after a report that SpaceX was seeking at least 80,000 U.S. cell sites to build a rival carrier.

Deutsche Telekom Gains as T-Mobile US Profit Jumps 27%, but Analysts See Few Fresh Surprises
sum: Deutsche Telekom shares rose 2.0% on Wednesday, lifted by unexpectedly strong quarterly figures from its US subsidiary T-Mobile US. The question for investors is whether that momentum can outlast the session — and on that point, the sell side is notably measured.

T-Mobile US reported net income of USD 3.5 billion for the third quarter of 2026, a 27% increase year on year. Adjusted free cash flow for the quarter came in at USD 5.1 billion, up 5% from the prior-year period. The carrier also raised its full-year guidance for adjusted free cash flow to a range of USD 18.7–18.8 billion — a target, not a result.

That distinction matters. An upgraded outlook can build confidence, but it only hardens into a durable case once subsequent quarters confirm it. The same logic applies to the operating detail: T-Mobile US said postpaid customer growth and average revenue per postpaid account both beat its original expectations, while it added 274,000 net postpaid accounts and posted adjusted EBITDA of USD 9.6 billion in the quarter. Customer momentum of that kind gives the raised cash-flow target more substance than a single earnings line alone.

JPMorgan, for its part, kept its "Overweight" rating and EUR 38 price target on Deutsche Telekom in a note dated Tuesday. Analyst Akhil Dattani wrote that the T-Mobile US figures and the adjusted annual targets were largely in line with expectations — a caveat that tempers any reading of the US results as a fresh re-rating catalyst.

Barclays offers a more cautious counterpoint. On October 20 the bank cut its price target on the stock from EUR 35 to EUR 32 while reaffirming its "Overweight" rating, pairing a lower valuation with a still-positive recommendation.

Sentiment has also been shaped by corporate strategy. According to Bloomberg, Deutsche Telekom has shelved plans for a full merger with T-Mobile US for now, a pause investors read as relief from potential dilution risk. Bloomberg, citing people familiar with the matter, reported that a later offer remains possible — so the pause is not a final abandonment. Any lift from reduced transaction risk is a different animal from an operational improvement, and could prove shorter-lived.

T-Mobile US raises cash outlook: what it means for T-Mobile US stock
sum: T-Mobile US (ISIN US8725901040) raised its full-year 2026 cash flow outlook after reporting third-quarter results on October 28, 2026. The T-Mobile Newsroom reported service revenue of USD 19.4 billion, up 6 percent from the prior-year quarter, while postpaid service revenue rose 9 percent to USD 16.3 billion.

T-Mobile added 274,000 postpaid accounts in the third quarter, taking the total to 35.0 million, 3 percent above the prior-year period. Postpaid average revenue per account increased 4 percent year over year to USD 155.73, and postpaid account churn was 1.09 percent.

Profitability also improved. Net income increased 27 percent year over year to USD 3.5 billion, diluted earnings per share rose 34 percent to USD 3.22, and core adjusted EBITDA grew 11 percent to USD 9.6 billion. Adjusted free cash flow reached USD 5.1 billion, up 5 percent from the third quarter of 2025.

Management lifted full-year adjusted free cash flow guidance to USD 18.7 billion-18.8 billion from USD 18.4 billion-18.8 billion. The midpoint therefore increased by USD 0.15 billion. Full-year core adjusted EBITDA guidance moved to USD 37.35 billion-37.45 billion from USD 37.1 billion-37.5 billion, while service revenue guidance was set at USD 76.8 billion, representing 8 percent growth.

The company also expects about 1.0 million postpaid net account additions in 2026. Management linked the outlook to continued postpaid growth, while noting that wholesale and prepaid trends will partly offset the improvement.

T-Mobile returned USD 3.5 billion to stockholders in the third quarter, including USD 2.4 billion in repurchases and USD 1.1 billion in dividends. The company declared a USD 1.17 quarterly dividend, a 15 percent increase, payable on December 10, 2026, to stockholders of record on November 25, 2026, as reported by Nasdaq.

T-Mobile US stock was trading at EUR 137.31 at Lang & Schwarz on October 29, 2026, at 12:32 p.m. CET. The company is listed on the NASDAQ under the ticker TMUS, and the reported quarter gives investors a current operating benchmark through account growth, service revenue and cash generation.

A report that SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) wants access to 80,000 U.S. cell sites is hitting every major national wireless carrier at once. Shares of T-Mobile (NASDAQ:TMUS) fell 5% to $150.74 during morning trading, a sign of how directly the SpaceX threat lands on its wireless business.

Meanwhile, AT&T (NYSE:T) stock is down 4% to $21.79, a smaller decline that still tracks T-Mobile's slide. Verizon Communications (NYSE:VZ) stock is trading at $43.70, down 3%, the most resilient of the national carriers.

Losses in the carriers are weighing on the sector fund that holds each of them. The Communication Services Select Sector SPDR ETF (NYSEARCA:XLC) is down 1% to $105.94; for broad-market context, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is down 0.5% to $759.90.

Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter, that SpaceX is in talks with at least one major cell tower owner to secure access to a large network of U.S. cell sites. Such a deal would move SpaceX a step closer to building a fourth nationwide wireless carrier to take on AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile in their home market. Starlink already serves over 13.6 million consumer subscribers worldwide, giving SpaceX an existing customer base to build from.

However, persistent high Treasury yields and Delta Air Lines lowering its full-year earnings guidance due to soaring jet fuel costs kept investors cautious. Telecom shares tumbled amid SpaceX’s low-band spectrum acquisition for Starlink Mobile, while Apple fell on reported iPhone production cuts. Meanwhile, OpenAI’s strong revenue outlook supported tech sentiment ahead of key consumer sentiment and agricultural data releases.

ASTS Stock Slides After-Hours As SpaceX Snags Grain Spectrum: Analyst Who Called The Deal Says ‘Ligado Is Next’
sum: - Roger Entner, who predicted the Starlink deal in August, said “Ligado is next,” putting AST’s agreements with Ligado for access to up to 45 MHz of spectrum in focus.
- AST had pursued Grain’s frequencies, but SpaceX’s deal leaves AST’s existing spectrum arrangements with AT&T and Verizon intact.
- Entner called the recent AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon satellite alliance a push for “an open standard, not an Elon standard.”

Shares of AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) slid 4% after hours on Thursday after SpaceX agreed to acquire nationwide spectrum AST had pursued, prompting telecom analyst Roger Entner, who predicted the Starlink deal in August, to say North American satcom firm Ligado Networks could be next.

ASTS stock fell 6% on Thursday to close at $56.93, its lowest close in over a month. Shares are down nearly 3% for the week, on track for a second consecutive weekly decline. AT&T (T), T-Mobile US (TMUS) and Verizon Communications (VZ) shares also each fell about 6% in overnight trading late Thursday.

Grain Management said on Thursday that SpaceX would acquire its entire nationwide 800 MHz spectrum portfolio, subject to Federal Communications Commission (FCC) approval and other conditions. Financial terms were not disclosed. The portfolio includes up to 14 megahertz of paired low-band spectrum. SpaceX said that the frequencies address a key remaining technical gap in Starlink Mobile’s effort to become a major U.S. mobile carrier.

In its announcement, SpaceX outlined a hybrid network combining satellites with terrestrial infrastructure. Its 2 GHz mid-band spectrum would supply high-bandwidth capacity, while the low-band frequencies would provide coverage designed to penetrate walls and reach devices inside buildings. Most existing mobile devices already support the band, the company said.

AT&T Teams Up With LifeMD for Virtual Health Care: Can it Aid Shares?
sum: AT&T Inc. T has added new healthcare benefits for its eligible wireless and fiber customers through a partnership with LifeMD, Inc. LFMD, offering complimentary access to virtual care and pharmacy services. The collaboration expands AT&T’s customer offerings by providing healthcare services alongside its wireless and fiber products.

Per the agreement, AT&T will provide more than 100 million eligible customers with a LifeMD membership worth $228 annually, waiving the regular $19 monthly fee. Customers can connect with healthcare providers for everyday health needs, obtain prescriptions and access pharmacy services, with many medications delivered directly through LifeMD’s pharmacy.

The company is offering the benefit through AT&T’s &More program, which provides members with savings and special deals. Customers must enroll to activate the complimentary membership and will pay only for the visits, prescriptions, or other services they use. The rollout will initially cover about 29 million AT&T customers in 11 states and is expected to expand nationwide in January 2027.
As demand for convenient telemedicine services continues to grow, the initiative supports AT&T’s efforts to broaden its customer benefits and strengthen engagement across its service ecosystem.

AT&T faces stiff competition from Verizon Communications, Inc. VZ and T-Mobile US, Inc. TMUS. Verizon is enhancing its healthcare technology offerings with artificial intelligence (AI)-powered solutions for telehealth and connected care. Its AI Connect platform helps healthcare organizations manage secure, real-time data flows. Verizon provides network solutions to support connected medical devices and healthcare facilities.

T-Mobile is strengthening its healthcare offerings with 5G and wireless technologies that support telehealth and virtual care. The company provides private and hybrid 5G networks for healthcare organizations, helping connect facilities, applications and medical devices. T-Mobile’s solutions also support patient monitoring, connected hospital operations and secure digital healthcare services.

Why T-Mobile Stock Dropped 11% Despite a Q2 Earnings Beat
sum: - With adjusted EPS of $3.27 beating estimates by 22% and EBIT margin expanding 230 basis points to 24.09%, T-Mobile’s profitability outran a slight 0.65% revenue miss against Street estimates of $22.94 billion.
- Q3 net postpaid account additions are guided to just 250,000, down sharply from Q2’s 277,000, as planned rate plan modernization work drives a temporary spike in churn.
- Raising full-year free cash flow guidance to $18.4 billion-$18.8 billion, T-Mobile pointed to lower cash income taxes as the primary driver of the $200 million increase at the midpoint.

- But the account growth story got complicated: CFO Peter Osvaldik acknowledged on the call that the modernization push would create “a temporary elevated account churn profile,” concentrated in accounts with fewer lines.
TMUS Beats on Profit but a Q3 Churn Warning Spooks the Stock

T-Mobile (TMUS) posted second quarter revenue of $22.79 billion, missing Street estimates of $22.94 billion by 0.65% and slipping 1.37% from the prior quarter. TMUS stock closed at $170.42 on July 23, down 10.75% in a single session, even as adjusted EPS of $3.27 beat estimates by 22.23% and climbed 14.90% year over year. Core adjusted EBITDA hit $9.54 billion against a $9.40 billion estimate, and EBIT margin expanded 230 basis points to 24.09% versus the 21.79% Street had modeled.

That gap between the headline miss and the underlying beat traces back to guidance. Management held full-year postpaid account net additions at 950,000 to 1,050,000, but flagged Q3 net adds of just 250,000, down from the 277,000 T-Mobile delivered in Q2. CFO Peter Osvaldik explained the drop directly on the Q2 2026 earnings call: “As part of our full year plan and guidance, we anticipated our Q3 rate plan modernization would result in a temporary elevated account churn profile and expect Q3 net postpaid account additions to be approximately 250,000.” He added that the churn hit lands mostly on accounts with fewer lines, meaning postpaid phone churn stays comparatively insulated.

The downward pressure on T-Mobile US (TMUS) shares, marked by notable intraday volatility, is primarily driven by a combination of strategic customer billing shifts and intensifying competitive headwinds in the satellite-to-cellular space.

First, T-Mobile has officially confirmed plans to streamline its wireless offerings by retiring thousands of legacy phone plans, including Simple Choice, T-Mobile One, and older Sprint plans. Long-time subscribers are being automatically migrated to newer, more expensive plans, which is expected to raise monthly rates. While this consolidation is intended to modernize operations and eventually lift average revenue per user (ARPU), the decision has triggered severe consumer backlash. Investors are highly concerned about a spike in subscriber churn, as affected customers may choose to defect to low-cost cable providers or alternative carriers, threatening the market-leading subscriber retention that has historically supported T-Mobile's premium valuation.

Second, sentiment is being weighed down by escalating threats of disruptive technological competition. Reports indicate that SpaceX is actively exploring a consumer mobile launch for its Starlink satellite service, potentially partnering with major telecom entities like Charter. This prospect of a direct satellite-to-consumer wireless competitor threatens to bypass traditional carrier networks and challenge T-Mobile's dominant position. Although T-Mobile previously posted strong quarterly financial metrics, these dual threats of increased near-term churn from legacy migrations and long-term direct-to-cell competition from SpaceX are prompting institutional investors to re-evaluate their exposure, driving the stock's downward volatility.
